stem: An asymptomatic 60-year-old man asks whether he should have PSA-based screening for prostate cancer. Which response best matches the current final USPSTF recommendation?

options.A: Recommend routine PSA screening for all adult men beginning at age 18.
options.B: Treat a single elevated PSA result as diagnostic of prostate cancer without further evaluation.
options.C: Discuss the potential benefits and harms of PSA-based screening and incorporate the client's values and preferences into an individual decision.
options.D: Recommend routine PSA-based screening for all men age 70 years and older.

rationale: The current final USPSTF recommendation states that for men aged 55 to 69 years, the decision to undergo periodic PSA-based prostate-cancer screening should be an individual one after discussion of potential benefits and harms and consideration of patient values and preferences. The USPSTF recommends against routine PSA-based screening in men 70 years or older. The prostate-screening recommendation is currently being updated, but as of August 16, 2026, the 2018 statement remains the current final recommendation. C is therefore correct.
educational_objective: Apply the current final USPSTF recommendation by using informed, individualized decision-making for PSA-based prostate-cancer screening in men aged 55 to 69 years.
source_document_title: Prostate Cancer: Screening — Final Recommendation Statement
source_version_date: Final recommendation May 8, 2018; update in progress; current final status rechecked 2026-08-16
source_locator: Recommendation Summary; Informed Decision Making; Clinical Considerations — men aged 55-69 and men age 70 years or older; In Progress page showing 2018 remains current final recommendation
source_claim_supported: For men aged 55-69, PSA screening is an individual decision after discussion of benefits and harms and patient preferences; routine PSA screening is not recommended for men 70 years or older. The recommendation update is still in progress.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed p.9, Health Promotion and Maintenance — provide age-appropriate preventive care, screening education, and health-promotion teaching
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — prostate cancer screening

source_original.stem: An asymptomatic 60-year-old man asks whether he should have PSA-based screening for prostate cancer. Which response best matches the current final USPSTF recommendation?

options.A: Recommend routine PSA screening for all adult men beginning at age eighteen
options.B: Treat one elevated PSA result as diagnostic of prostate cancer without workup
options.C: Discuss individual PSA screening benefits and harms with men aged 55 to 69
options.D: Recommend routine PSA screening for all men aged seventy years and older

source_original.rationale: The current final USPSTF recommendation (May 8, 2018; update in progress as of 2026-08-14) recommends individualized decision-making for PSA-based screening in men aged 55–69 after discussion of benefits and harms. It recommends against routine PSA-based screening in men aged 70 years or older.
source_original.source_detail: Final recommendation May 8, 2018: individualized PSA decision age 55–69; recommend against routine screening age ≥70; update in progress, accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Verified that the 2018 statement remains the current final USPSTF recommendation on 2026-08-16 despite an update being in progress, strengthened the shared-decision wording to include values/preferences, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy.

audit_findings.source_authority: USPSTF current final recommendation; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: USPSTF In Progress page still directs users to the 2018 current final recommendation; no newer final statement identified as of 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final wording exactly reflects the grade C individual-decision recommendation for ages 55-69 and the grade D recommendation against routine screening at 70+.

distractor_audit.A: No USPSTF recommendation supports universal adult screening from age 18.
distractor_audit.B: PSA is a screening test and one elevated result does not by itself diagnose cancer.
distractor_audit.D: Contradicts the recommendation against routine screening in men 70+.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The stem specifies a 60-year-old asymptomatic man, placing him squarely in the 55-69 shared-decision group; C is uniquely correct.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are screening/interpretation strategies; the key is determined by guideline knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance is appropriate for age-based preventive screening counseling.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked the current final recommendation page and the USPSTF In Progress page, specifically verified that no replacement final statement had been published by 2026-08-16, and confirmed C remained uniquely correct.
